# Manual Meter Input

This functionality is only available for gas meters.

## External Volume Interface

Use the External Volume Interface to manually enter data for any gas meter, including external volume meters. (A meter is defined as an External Volume meter by enabling this option from the [Imports tab](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Imports%20Tab.md) of the Meter Editor.) Once the data is imported, you can exit the External Volume Interface and view the data from the Volume Editor.

This import screen differs from other meter import screens because users can manually enter energy values.

The meter drop-down defaults to "External Volume Meters Only." To select a gas meter from the meter drop-down, the "Can enter data for any meter" System Configuration option must be enabled.

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Entering Data">

<div class="procedure">

To manually enter data using the External Volume Interface:

1.  Go to **Import** \> **Manual Entry** \> **Meter Input**.
2.  Select the **External Volume Meters Only** option to filter the meter drop-down by external volume meters only.
3.  Click the **Browse** button to find a text file to import (example: C:\data\01301-July.txt), or type the file path into the edit box.
4.  Select the meter number or meter name from the drop-down.
5.  Select **Contract Month** or **Contract Day(s)** for the date range.
6.  Click **OK**.
7.  To enter daily data, check the **Enter daily data** option. To enter monthly data, leave the **Enter daily data** option unchecked.
8.  Enter the volume, energy, heating value, differential pressure, static pressure, and/or temperature. For positive displacement meters, enter the appropriate data for the applicable dates.
9.  Leave the **Do not calculate heating value** option unchecked to have FLOWCAL calculate a heating value automatically.
10. Select the **Enter Mass** option to enter mass.
11. Select values for the contract day and hour.
12. Select the data resolution (15-minute, 1 hour, or 1 day).
13. Select **Leading** or **Trailing** for the data span.
14. Click the **Analysis** tab to manually enter analysis data.
15. Click the **Characteristics** tab to manually enter characteristics data.
16. Click **Import**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 686;height: 497;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Manual Data Entry Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Manual Data Entry screen:

- **Analysis** – Click this button to open the source assigned to the meter for the date range selected.
- **Change** – Click this button to change meter number or data range.
- **For DP, Pres., and Temp.**
  - **Fill blanks with monthly value** – When a range total differential pressure, pressure, and/or temperature is entered, select this option and click Fill In to automatically populate the same values for all daily records containing volume or pulses.
  - **Fill blanks with previous day’s value** – When a differential pressure, pressure, and/or temperature is entered for a daily record, select this option and click Fill In to automatically populate the same values for all subsequent daily records containing volume or pulses.
- **Tab Order**
  - **Full Row** – Select this option to tab across the entire row, left to right, from Volume to Temperature.
  - **Half Row** – Select this option to tab across the left side of the row, from Volume to Heating Value. Upon reaching the last row or daily record, pressing Tab will navigate to the right half of the row, from Differential Pressure to Temperature.

</div>
